utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Call the case on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-98-32/1-R77.2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Jelena Rasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could just have appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honour. Paul Rogers and Kyle Wood representing the Prosecution, together with our Case Manager Ms. Jasmina Bosnjakovic. And, Your Honour, Mr. Wood will be conducting the hearing this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning to everybody in the courtroom. I'm Mira Tapuskovic, Defence counsel of the accused, Jelena Rasic. Present today with me is Liane Aronchick, an attorney from the United States of America, who is our Legal Assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I think I've run out of B/C/S now, so I shall have to start listening to the translation. Do all parties have a copy of the proposed agenda and timetable? Are there any initial observations before we go into the matters on agenda? No. Right. Well, the pending motions, the position is that there are two motions pending. Time ran out, to be blunt, on the 1st of February. But unless there are any objections, I'm intending to unilaterally extend the time-limits under Rule 126 to deal with those issues. It's just not been possible as a result of the make-up of the Court and the duties of other Judges involved to get everybody in the same place at the same time to fully determine the issues, although I think we can perhaps deal with them with a reasonable amount of consensus today. Are there any objections to the extending of time-limits for the judgements in those cases? No. Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Now, of course, time-limits are principally designed to stop delays where there are long and complex cases and, of course, where people are remanded in custody, features which, frankly, don't apply to this case. Let's deal with the issue of the indictment first and the Defence motion. I'm going to make my own position blunt. It doesn't, of course, in any sense tie the other Judges, nor does it predicate an eventual decision for that reason; it's a majority decision. But my own view is that the indictment does provide a prima facie case and complies with the Rules; had it not done so, I wouldn't have confirmed it. However, I can see, although I think it may be formulistic, that there could be an advantage, although it seems to me that the accused must know the nature of the case that she faces which is the -- and the nature of the allegations which she faces. It would be extraordinary if she didn't at this stage, especially being represented, as she is, by experienced counsel. But when I first looked at the indictment, one thing that went through my head was that it could be perfected simply by adding these words after paragraph 2 on Count 1: "Knowing or believing the said statement to be false." That makes it clear beyond a peradventure. It seems to me to be absolutely clear anyway from the nature of the case, and one could read into that. Likewise, on -- paragraph 16, under Count 5, and paragraph 9, under Counts 3 and 4, the same words, simply: "Knowing or believing the said statement to be false, or said statements to be false." Under Count 2, it seems to me it's inherent from the words "encouraged and ... persuaded" that the accused knew that the procuration was a procuration alleged of false statements. Any observations as to that position from either party?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Of course, this is something that would be addressed more fully in a pre-trial brief and that's something that may address some of your concerns. But also, that is something we'll reflect upon and consider more fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Taking the hypothetical case, Ms. Tapuskovic, that that was the addendum or addition to the indictment, would that satisfy any concerns that you have? It seems to make it plain beyond a peradventure what the accusation is.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Very well. Put that to one side at the moment then. I can hear from the Prosecution whether they adopt that suggestion. If they do, it may be that the motion can be withdrawn without further ado, but ... Now disclosure, Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure, what is the status for that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: The Prosecution's records reflect that the 66(A)(ii) disclosure is essentially complete Your Honour, with the exception of four witnesses, two of which -- well, that are subject to request for waiver. Those will be provided to the Defence as soon as -- if and when they become available. With the exception of those, all the 66(A)(ii) disclosure has been complete. Ms. Tapuskovic and I discussed one outstanding matter on Wednesday. One 92 bis statement that she had not received, and I sent that to her that same day. I believe she's received that. I think that concludes the 66(A)(ii) disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can say that the Defence is very pleased with the cooperation with the OTP so far. Since I was appointed Defence counsel, I have, on several occasions, communicated with my learned friend, either in person or by e-mail, and the cooperation has been very fruitful. The disclosure has been completed except for this matter. And we had a meeting two days ago and my request was granted immediately. So I have no objections to the disclosure process so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Very well. Any attempts or any successful attempts or otherwise to reach agreement on any factual matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: This is something that we discussed immediately before this hearing started. It's -- I don't want to put words in the mouth of Ms. Tapuskovic, who can speak for herself obviously. But it's my understanding, the Prosecution's understanding, that she's still in the phase of investigating the allegations. But we did discuss some matters that we might able to reach agreement on. That seems to be something that we'll be able to do in the fullness of discussion as soon as Ms. Tapuskovic is satisfied she has investigated the case fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. As I have informed the OTP team, we are nearing the end of our investigation and then we will be ready to negotiate which facts can be considered as agreed. So at some time in mid-February, we will be in that stage, when we will be able to tell which facts we agree on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, that's a very satisfactory time-scale. Let's turn to the proposed work-plan, giving potential for dates to be fixed. The preliminary motions we can set aside for the moment. Rule 66 material seems to be in hand. Pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: The Prosecution anticipates, Your Honour, that we would be able to produce a pre-trial brief within about four weeks from the determination of the outstanding motions. Obviously some of the decisions that are made on those motions will affect how the pre-trial brief looks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Agreed. And the date for the Defence brief is going to be predicated by the service of the Prosecution pre-trial brief, so we can hold that in abeyance for the moment as far as fixing a date is concerned. If we can, can we say, for a date for the pre-trial brief, you say a month after the motions are determined, but to try and give slightly more structure to it, can we aim, please, for Friday, the 29th of April?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that -- as my colleague said, it's very generous. I think we can do that. And obviously I didn't mention, but the exhibit list and the witness list would follow the same timetable and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, that's -- that's -- I make it plain. That's the last date. If it can be available before that, all well and good. But I take into account the fact that Easter intervenes, and I know that some of my fellow Judges are not going to be present in The Hague in that intervening period, so I'm afraid my generosity is tempered by reality. Any observations, Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I have no remarks. The deadline is fine with us. Now the question is how much time will you give us to draft our 65 ter documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: How long are you asking for?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will need three weeks after the reception of the OTP pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Very well. Taking the -- the pessimistic assumption that it's the 29th of April, that gives us by Friday, the 20th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is acceptable for the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, a number of witnesses is going to be, I think, at the moment a fluid assessment. And the number of Defence witness, were there to be any, is something that one, at the moment, can't calculate for various reasons. Let's take a worse case scenario that this matter goes to a full trial with all of the witnesses that both parties presently anticipate. Can you give an estimated length of trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In the Prosecution's case, at most we anticipate having to call up to 19 witnesses. We have identified that 11 of those, with the Court's leave obviously, could be presented via 92 bis. Obviously this is not taking into consideration that some agreements might be able to made on some of these smaller matters. Seven of those, the Prosecution anticipates or would seek to tender via 92 ter. And there is one expert witness that the Prosecution has noted. Taking all that into account, if we could proceed on the 92 bis/92 ter path, the Prosecution anticipates we could maybe do in seven -- five to seven court days, the length of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the assumption that the Prosecution case took seven working days and that the Defence was required to present their entire Defence, what's the longest period you would have thought it was likely to last, Ms. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no problem with giving an estimate now. At this moment, the Defence expects to call four viva voce witnesses and a Rule 92 bis witness. As far as we're concerned, the Defence case would not take more than four or five days. But as you have said, Your Honour, at the beginning, this is, of course, approximative. However, we don't expect much deviation from this estimate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: And if I could just add, Your Honour, to clarify: That estimate is -- doesn't take into account if the three main witnesses were to testify viva voce. That would change the timetable obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: It appears to me though that we're looking at a trial that's going to take probably in the order of 15 working days at a maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: I think that's fair to say, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. That ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I'm reminded, in the necessity of serving the evidence of an expert witness, that should be done at the latest a week before the service of the Defence -- the Prosecution pre-trial brief, which would be the 22nd of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: And obviously much earlier if that's feasible, which I -- no doubt it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: It is. In fact, the report of the expert has already been disclosed to Ms. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Ah, so be it. Any other matters at this stage that the Court can assist with?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution's view, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to raise one issue with you and the OTP team. For that purpose, I would ask for us to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Well, I take into account what you say. At the moment, I don't think it impacts upon the trial. If things change, so be it. I'm proposing to fix a date of the next Status Conference, to make sure that we have it in mind from now, which would be Friday, unfortunately, Friday the 13th, but Friday, the 13th of May, 2011. Any difficulties with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: My colleague is just suggesting, Your Honour, that it might best to have the next Status Conference after the Defence pre-trial brief has been filed. At that point we'll have both briefs and we'll be in a better position to know what comes next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: It's a good point. I just don't want to allow for too much -- well, as one knows, it has to be within -- it should be within 120 days. If no objection is taken, if there's any slippage over that date, that's a requirement which is really in place for those people who are remanded in custody, to make sure that they are not remanded for too long, as well as for keeping a grip on the timetable of the trial. But on the -- on the assumption that the Defence brief is not in fact filed until 20th of May, which, as I say, as with the Prosecution brief, that's a latest date, not an earliest date. For the moment, let's fix the next Status Conference to the 27th of May, with the understanding that that can be brought forward, if it's possible to do so, assuming that all briefs have been filed before that date. But at least it gives us a day to work towards. Any other matters?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I would just like to say that I agree with the OTP proposal, that our Status Conference should be scheduled for after the Defence brief has been filed. And we will do our best to do it by the deadline just given by you, Your Honours. We don't have any other remarks at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: No. Well, thank you very much. It seems obvious that this is a reasonable collegiate effort between the parties in this case, which I encourage. When I was Defence counsel, I was on the -- that was the Defence representative on the Rules Committee, and I tried to encourage the creation of agreed facts, documentary agreed facts, which is what I was used to doing in the United Kingdom. I think I might have been overly enthusiastic, because it was shortly after that that Rule 92 was imposed. But I disclaim any responsibility for that whatsoever. Thank you very much. And the hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
